headline: Google Research links agentic lab control with closed-loop molecular discovery
summary: A Google Research overview dated October 16 links three papers on AI-assisted wet-lab work. VERID uses a persistent semantic digital twin, simulation gate and synchronized execution traces; its demonstrations use dye and water to expose physical lab errors and recover from faults. A separate aptamer study reports three design-test rounds on myoglobin and alpha-thrombin: new-design hit rates reached 33.5% and 42.1%, respectively, after intermediate specificity failures; strictly de novo thrombin binders remained low-micromolar. A FAP binder-design study combines target-region excision with agent-guided parameter and compute allocation. For one 719-residue target under a shared GPU budget, the human-agent arm reported a 9.33% computational hit rate using 77.18 GPU-hours versus 5.06% using 132.87 GPU-hours for the human baseline; the authors report four representative enriched yeast-display clones with apparent 3.0–9.1 nM affinities. All results are first-party paper reports without independent reproduction. They concern specific targets and workflows, not general autonomous science or demonstrated therapeutic efficacy.
